# Architecture review: roadmap since 0.11.0 (read-only)

Scope: open PRs 469, 470, 472, 474, 475, 477-483 and merged 468, 473 (plus 476 inside 469). Read in final form from the
remote refs as of this review (the fetch was blocked by the sandbox, so the refs are the last fetched ones, 5 to 120
minutes old). Nothing built or run. Branch shorthands used in anchors:

- `co` = origin/feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default (469; contains 472 and 476 and the picked/notable fixes)
- `ro` = origin/feat/relevance-output (483; stacks 470, 473, 477-480 on an **older** 469, 6b9a187b)
- `sc` = origin/feat/scheduler-priority-and-cancel (481; 482 merged into it)
- `hb` = origin/feat/one-shot-heap-budget (474), `sp` = origin/feat/structural-parity-utility-and-generics (475),
  `jx` = origin/feat/jsx-evidence-in-extractor (470)

## Ranked findings

Value/cost order. Tags: **do-now** (cheap, removes risk), **do-next** (a slice), **skip** (not worth it).

1. **do-now: relevance evidence is not a recorded dependency, so watch and lazy answers go stale.** `ro`
   `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs:271-287` gathers `relevance_inputs::evidence` *after*
   `resolve_component_tracked`, outside `deps::recording` (`resolver/mod.rs:931-938`). The evidence reads other
   files: call sites of every consumer (`relevance_inputs.rs:51-61`), forwarding targets through imports
   (`:81-92`), and the props type's declarations (`:67-79`). `pipeline/revision.rs:559-562` keeps a component whose
   `depends_on` is untouched, so a page that adds `<Button className>` never refreshes Button's `relevance` in watch
   or the lazy session (`revision/lazy.rs:417`). The ADR's Consequences call for whole-project invalidation here,
   and the code does not invalidate at all. Fix: gather evidence inside the recording closure and mark call-site
   evidence as depending on every file with JSX usages (or on a "project JSX" pseudo-dependency). Test: see item 13.

2. **do-now: `decide` contradicts ADR 0028 for passed ambient members.** `ro` `relevance/mod.rs:222-223`: `passed`
   puts any member at the floor in `rows`, ambient or not. The ADR says an ambient member passed at the floor goes in
   the layer's `used` list. The test pins the wrong rule: `a_prop_passed_at_a_fifth_of_the_call_sites_is_a_typed_row`
   (`:474-488`, ambient `b` expected `Row`). On shadcn, `className` at 243 components would become a typed row each,
   which is the cost the ADR's `used` list exists to avoid. Fix: `passed && member.ambient` goes to `used`. Either fix
   the test or amend the ADR on purpose.

3. **do-now: schema 8 is spent on a shape the ADR did not decide.** ADR 0028 "Output" bumps schema 8 for

10. **do-next: unify picked keys (four readers of `Pick`).** These all read `Pick`: the structural resolver
    `resolver/alias.rs:81-96`, structural parity `sp` `resolver/evaluate.rs` `utility_fields` (Pick in key order),

    `PropsType::pick/keys`.

11. **do-next: split along seams that the ADR's serial waves already fight over.** S3, S4 and S5 all edit
    `on_demand.rs` "after" each other, and T7 and S1 both edit `types/semantic.rs`.
    - `sc` `semantic/src/on_demand.rs` (1,109 lines): move `Queue<T>` (`:160-215`, pure) to `on_demand/queue.rs` and

    - `co` `core/src/types/semantic.rs` (1,144 lines): move the provider protocol (`SemanticTarget`,
      `SemanticProvider`, `Priority`, `SharedPriority`, `Delivery`, `SourceChange`; `:164-305`) to
      `types/semantic/provider.rs`. Move the layering (`layer_checker_props`, `LayerFacts`, `Layering`, `Structural`,
      `checker_sources`, `keeps`, `move_notable`, `unconverted_type`; `:386-697`) to a `collapse` module next to
      `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` and `CollapseContext`. The collapse decision then has one home instead of
      options.rs + semantic.rs + resolver/mod.rs.
    - `ro` `core/src/resolver/mod.rs` (1,379 lines): move `can_collapse`/`collapses`/`one_layer_per_collapsed_source`/
      `declares_large_source` (`:585-656`) into that same `collapse` module (resolver side).
    - `sc` `packages/storybook/src/background.ts` (252 lines): move the pure `Prefetched`/`prefetchStep`/`seen`

      the `lifecycle.ts` reducer pattern.
    - Skip: `extractor/body_facts.rs` (634, one visitor, one job), `resolver/evaluate.rs` (`sp` 1,099; the utility
      evaluation is cohesive with `literal_set`/`mapped_keys`), `convert.rs` (2,018 lines, but its change here is
      small; split with S4's memo-lifetime work if at all).

12. **do-next: dead code and unused evidence fields violate "wire or don't define".**
    - `ro` `extractor/story_args.rs` (299 lines, `#![cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))]` at `:12`).
    - `relevance/call_sites.rs:44, :95` (story args) and `:113` (`CallSites::used`, a second floor beside
      `CallSites::at_floor` at `relevance/mod.rs:175`: a duplicated rule kept alive by a test).
    - `Evidence::story_args` (always `Vec::new()`, `relevance/mod.rs:43`).
    - `Body::defaulted` (always `Vec::new()`, `relevance_inputs.rs:40`; defaults arrive through
      `PropsType::defaulted` instead).
    - `Attribute::Named::prop` ("given no weight", `relevance/mod.rs:145-147`).

    Delete them, or wire stories discovery in T4. The `expect(dead_code)` reason "wired by T7" is already false: T7 is
    this PR.

13. **do-next: the test model for the next bug class.** The likely next reviewer-found class is **stale derived
    state**: an answer kept across an edit whose derivation read something not in its dependency set. Item 1 is the
    first instance. Others are call-site counts cached in `ResolutionContext::relevance_sites` (`OnceLock`) and the
    scheduler's re-ask after an edit (item 15).

    Model: a `watch_equals_fresh` model test in `crates/core/tests`. It builds a generated project (the
    `relevance_model.rs` generator plus a consumer file, a forwarding wrapper and a story), applies a random sequence
    of edits to it (add or remove a call site in a consumer, change a forward target's own props, rename an export,
    edit the props type), and after each edit asserts that `WatchSession` and the lazy session produce the same
    output as a fresh `extract()`, `relevance` and layers included.

    The checker oracle catches type errors, not this. The second model is `relevance_model.rs` with `@types/react`
    and `@react-types/shared` fixtures: today its generated sources never exercise `ambient`, so item 5 cannot fail
    it.

14. **do-next: an `Exact | Declined` helper for speculative resolution.** `sp` `resolver/named.rs:247-283` resolves
    utility fields in a branch, then on decline hand-clears `branch.diagnostics`, `shared_diagnostics` and
    `named_unevaluated` before `absorb`, while keeping recorded dependencies. That is three fields by convention, and
    a fourth `ResolveState` field will be missed. Fix: `ResolveState::attempt(|branch| -> Option<T>)`, which commits
    everything on `Some`, and on `None` keeps only `deps`. `add_absent`'s factory branch (`ro` `resolver/mod.rs:1008,
    1026-1031`) is a second user. A full `Exact | Declined` result enum would be over-engineering: an `Option` plus

15. **do-next: two owners for "an edit supersedes a prefetch".** Rust `SemanticHook::invalidate` cancels every
    pending request nobody waits for (`sc` `pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:189-200`). TS then infers the edit from

    neighbours are never re-asked. Fix: the hook marks cancelled-by-edit neighbour requests "re-ask at next revision"
    itself, or exposes the generation so TS does not reconstruct it. At minimum, add a fast-check model test for
    `prefetchStep` against a one-line spec: after any event sequence, the keys live at the newest revision equal the
    current list's asked keys.

16. **do-next: the scheduler's priority encoding.** `sc` `types/semantic.rs:240-300` packs class plus cancel into an

    `Queue::next` (`on_demand.rs:186`) rebuilds the whole deque on each pick: O(n) per pick, O(n²) to drain a
    whole-project fill. A type-state queue is over-engineering. Instead, after the split in item 11, add a property
    test over random push/raise/cancel/pick sequences against a reference model (sort by (class, arrival), with the
    starvation rule). Replace the wildcard with `2 => Background, _ => unreachable-safe default` plus a `debug_assert`,

1. **Duplicated decisions.** Found in four places:
   - Ambient / React-declared: three predicates (item 5).
   - Picked keys: four readers (item 10).
   - Whole-props spread meaning: extractor vs `decide` (item 9).
   - Call-site floor: `CallSites::used` vs `at_floor` (item 12).

   Fine as is:
   - The collapse decision: one owner, `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses`, called by the resolver
     (`ro` `resolver/mod.rs:602-617`) and by `checker_sources`.
   - Notable props: one name list, `notable_html_attrs`, used in `co` `semantic.rs:488, 633` and in the resolver. It

     won has already decided.
2. **Trait / type-state.** Worth it: one sink for relevance (item 6), `ResolveState::attempt` (item 14), and a

   (`co` `semantic.rs:584-607`) is justified, since it has two real impls.
3. **Size.** See item 11.
4. **Visibility / API.**
   - New `pub` items crossing crates are justified: `Layering`, `LayerFacts`, `unconverted_type`,
     `merge_semantic_in`, `SharedPriority::cancel`.
   - Three public merge entry points (`merge_semantic`, `_with`, `_in`; `co` `semantic.rs:1060-1080`) should become

   - `RelevanceEvidence` is a public field on a wire type (item 6).
   - `HeapBudget::new` and `MAX_HEAP_BUDGET` should not be `pub` (item 18).
   - The napi surface grows by `sessionCancel` plus the `relevance` map. `sessionCancel` is wired and tested

   - Output names are camelCase and consistent. The `relevance` shape departs from ADR 0028 and from the contract's
     own pattern of `skip_serializing_if` for advisory fields (`degradedBy`): it is always written, `{}` when empty.
5. **Errors, naming, docs, dead code.**
   - Errors: the panic guard around evidence is right (`pipeline/mod.rs:273-283`). The release-silent filter is
     item 7.
   - Naming: `AsToday` (item 3), `Lane` (item 17), `merge_semantic_in`.
   - Style rules: names are `String` rather than the rule's `CompactString` throughout `relevance/*`. There is

   - Rustdoc: new `pub fn`s lack `# Examples` (`Layering::of`, `HeapBudget::machine`, `SharedPriority::cancel`). That

   - Dead code: item 12.
   - Harness: `collapse_model.rs`, `relevance_model.rs`, `size.rs` and `resolve.rs` in `crates/semantic/tests` each

1	# 0028. Show the props evidence makes relevant, and schedule the checker by what will be shown
2	
3	**Status:** Proposed **Date:** 2026-11-15
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Every surface returns every prop the checker resolves, minus what a collapsed layer hides. That is useless to Storybook and to agents: Chakra's `Button` had about 1,141 argTypes before the collapse-by-relevance PR (`feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default`) and 146 after it, and the rows still hidden are the ones consumers pass. Measured on origin/main 7b8f6d0d with the checker (trail 405 T5, `caliper-fixtures/shrink/relevance-baseline.md`), the share of the props a component's call sites pass that the output lists is 0.43 on shadcn (mean over 408 components; median 0.50), 0.86 on Mantine, 0.91 on ant-design and 0.96 on react-spectrum. Nearly every miss is a DOM attribute in a collapsed `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer (shadcn: `className` alone on 243 components), and those layers carry `htmlElement` with no `members` and `totalProps` 0, so a reader cannot tell what is inside them. Today's choices come from size and from name lists (`resolver/ambient.rs`'s `*StyleProps`, `GlobalDOMEvents` clauses; `notable_html_attrs` in `react_types.rs:462`), which the owner rules out.
8	
9	The checker's cost follows what it converts, not what is shown. A whole-project `extract` of Chakra's own repository built 42 GB of `PropType` trees converting its style system (`shrink/chakra-memory.md`), and the only memory guard (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:93`) reads the checker's arenas (`crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:169`), not the converter's heap, and only between requests (`on_demand.rs:643`).
10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	### A. Relevance decides what is shown, from evidence
14	
15	The owner's rules: returning all resolved props is useless for Storybook and agents; relevance decides what to show; it is derived from evidence, with no name lists; agent output is narrowed later.
16	
17	**Signals.** Each prop a component's props type reaches gets evidence from four places.
18	
19	- **The props type.** A member the props type declares itself is always shown. So is each key of `Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'>`, named on purpose; `Omit<X, 'k'>` says only that `k` is gone, nothing about the rest. A member that redeclares or narrows a base member is the component's own. A required member is shown (a story cannot render without it), and so is one with a `@default` tag or a destructuring default in the body (the component handles it). JSDoc and a literal-union type do not show a member on their own: as promoters they would list every documented member of a style system; they order the shown rows (open question 1).
20	- **Spreads in the body** (T1's `ComponentMapping::body`). `{...rest}` on a DOM tag passes the ambient DOM attributes: no evidence, ignored. A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
21	- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.
22	- **Unknown.** When `handed_on` is true, `reads` is incomplete (T1's contract), and the body says nothing: never guessed. The member falls back to today's single collapse decision with the reaching count (`CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` in the collapse PR; on main it is still `ResolutionContext::collapses`, `resolver/mod.rs:595`, by declared count, so `decide` is wired only after that PR merges), so missing evidence never hides more than today.
23	
24	**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. Each lane computes the bit for each prop and hands it to `decide` in `Evidence` (`is_react_declared` is private to `caliper-docgen-semantic`, which core does not depend on); `decide` never recomputes it, and a model test in the style of the collapse PR's `collapse_model.rs` holds the two lanes to the same bits. `ambient.rs`'s name clauses and `notable_html_attrs` stay as the unknown-evidence fallback until the T5 gate shows evidence replaces them; then they are deleted (slice R9).
25	
26	**Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.
27	
28	- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
29	- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
30	- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.
31	
32	**Output.** A collapsed `InheritedLayer` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:83`) gains `used`: the names of its members that evidence put forward, written once as a name list (ADR 0018), not as typed rows. Universal props such as `className`, `style` and `id` cost a name each instead of a row each. A `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer also gets its `members`, so a reader can check `used` against it. No per-prop flag in this ADR: the row/layer split already says shown or not, and why a row is shown is for the agent output, deferred. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 7 to 8 (ADR 0017), with the RDT view, the JSON schema, `binding.d.ts` and a changeset.
33	
34	**Consumers.** The Storybook addon makes argTypes from rows, then one name-only row per `used` name with the layer as its category; an option (`relevance: 'all'`) asks for the expanded output, which is today's `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. CLI JSON and TOON carry the same output. Agent output keeps its current form until the agent flow is narrowed.
35	
36	**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. Call-site evidence is computed from half of the files (by path hash) and coverage is measured on the other half, so the gate does not pass by construction. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.
37	
38	- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.
39	- Rows shown fall: the median rows per component does not rise on any corpus (Mantine 77, Spectrum 74, shadcn 3, antd 17), and total rows fall on Mantine and Spectrum. Chakra `Button`'s typed rows stay at or under 146 (its `used` names come on top and are reported apart).
40	- These targets are proposals. Only the extra-entry costs above were measured; the fall in rows is not predicted.
41
